answer: A Sybil-resistant economy can use synchronous, randomized peer liveness checks. Each epoch, agents are randomly paired and must complete a short interactive exchange within a narrow window — like a violet signal flashed at an unpredictable moment that a raven partner must answer before its ember fades. One operator cannot attend dozens of sessions at once, so each fake identity costs real, simultaneous attention and scheduling. Missed or duplicated responses lower trust, and repeated failures revoke the identity's right to transact.
